newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end higher on position-squaring.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end higher on position-squaring.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended higher as traders evened up positions ahead of the much-anticipated Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting Tuesday, traders said.
Japan's Autumn Equinox holiday and the Yom Kippur holiday on Monday kept trading limited to position-squaring, they said.
Talk that a Washinton advisory firm is forecasting the Fed Reserve will not raise rates at the FOMC meeting contributed to a bout of shortcovering around midday, traders said.
But volume was too thin to generate much upside momentum, and the light volume only exaggerated the midday moves of T-bonds and Eurodollars.
"Locals were trying to get things moving in here, but it just didn't work," one floor source said.
Other than one U.S. firm buying about 400 December T-bonds, and several U.S. firms each buying 1,000 March Eurodollar contracts, dealer activity was quiet, traders said.
Volume was estimated at 47,000 for December Eurodollars and was estimated at 51,000 for March Eurodollars.
March rose to 93.92, above Thursday's high at 93.90, while both December T-bonds and December Eurodollars remained within Thursday's ranges.

At the end of pit trade, December bonds were up 03/32 at 107-24/32, 10-year notes were up 03/32 at 106-11/32, December Eurodollars were steady at 94.06, March Eurodollars were up one basis point at 93.89 and March T-bills were also one bps higher at 94.44.
